beats: Same seventy thousand dollar salary. Last year, a refund. This year, you owe? Let's investigate three years.
Year one: one job, plus a six thousand dollar RRSP. At about thirty-three percent, that's a refund of about two thousand dollars.
Year two: same job, no RRSP. Payroll is built to land close to your actual tax. Refund: almost zero.
Year three: two jobs, thirty-five thousand each. Each payroll thinks it's your only job, so each gives you the basic personal amount. Under-withheld: about fifty-three hundred dollars.
The twist: your tax barely moved. What changed was what got withheld. A refund isn't a bonus. It's your own money coming back.
Check box twenty-two on your T4 against the total payable on your notice. Two jobs? On the second TD1, claim zero, or ask for extra tax off each cheque.
